note: West Virginia funnels every report of suspected abuse or neglect - of children and of vulnerable adults alike - through one Centralized Intake, staffed every hour of every day of the year. Its counseling board is candid about the limit on what a complaint can achieve: it can suspend, revoke or reprimand a licence, but it cannot recover a penny for you.

civil_injury.summary: Two years from the injury for personal injury, which includes assault, battery and negligence. Courts treat false imprisonment as a one-year claim.
civil_injury.quote: (b) within two years next after the right to bring the same shall have accrued if it be for damages for personal injuries; and (c) within one year next after the right to bring the same shall have accrued if it be for any other matter
civil_injury.note: The statute does not name assault, battery or false imprisonment. The one-year period for false imprisonment (and defamation) under 55-2-12(c) comes from case law, which I found only through secondary sources and did not read directly. West Virginia courts also apply a general discovery rule to accrual.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: For someone injured as a child, the same number of years (usually two) starts at 18. No claim can be brought more than 20 years after the injury. West Virginia's special longer deadline in this section is for childhood sexual abuse only.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: the same may be brought within the like number of years after his or her becoming of full age or sane that is allowed to a person having no such impediment ... except that it shall in no case be brought after 20 years from the time when the right accrues.
civil_minor_tolling.note: Subsection (a), the childhood sexual abuse provision amended by 2020 HB 4559, is excluded from this general rule and was not researched. I found no childhood-abuse extension in 55-2-15 for non-sexual physical abuse.

civil_government_claims.summary: Suits against a county, city, school board or other political subdivision must be filed within two years of the injury (or of its discovery), and a child still gets the extra time until 18. Before suing a state agency, you must mail written notice to the agency head and the Attorney General at least 30 days in advance.
civil_government_claims.citation: W. Va. Code § 29-12A-6(a) (political subdivisions); W. Va. Code § 55-17-3(a) (state agencies)
civil_government_claims.quote: (a) An action against a political subdivision to recover damages for injury ... shall be brought within two years after the cause of action arose or after the injury, death or loss was discovered or reasonably should have been discovered, whichever last occurs
civil_government_claims.note: 29-12A-6(b) would limit tolling for minors injured under age 10. In Whitlow v. Board of Education of Kanawha County (W. Va. 1993) the court held that 29-12A-6 violates equal protection 'to the extent that it denies to minors the benefit of' the general tolling statute, 55-2-15. I confirmed this from a CourtListener search summary (https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/1252879/whitlow-v-bd-of-educ-of-kanawha-cty/), not a full read. 55-17-3(a)(1) requires written notice by certified mail 'at least 30 days prior to the institution of an action against a governmental agency', and the limitation is tolled for 30 days after notice (https://code.wvlegislature.gov/55-17-3/). Recovery against the state itself is generally limited to its liability insurance or goes through the Legislative Claims Commission. That was not researched in detail.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: No time limit for felony child abuse: West Virginia has no statute of limitations for felonies. Misdemeanor child abuse must be charged within one year.
criminal_child_abuse.citation: W. Va. Code § 61-11-9 (limits misdemeanors and perjury only); W. Va. Code § 61-8D-3 (child abuse)
criminal_child_abuse.quote: A prosecution for committing or procuring another person to commit perjury shall be commenced within three years next after the perjury was committed. A prosecution for a misdemeanor shall be commenced within one year after the offense was committed
criminal_child_abuse.note: The 'no limit' comes from the absence of any felony limitation: 61-11-9 sets periods only for perjury and misdemeanors. Under 61-8D-3(b) and (c), child abuse by a parent, guardian, custodian or 'person in a position of trust' is a felony when it causes serious bodily injury or creates a substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury. That wording would cover program staff. Abuse creating a substantial risk of bodily injury is a misdemeanor under (d)(1), with one year (https://code.wvlegislature.gov/61-8D-3/).

criminal_felony_assault.summary: No time limit for felony malicious or unlawful wounding. Misdemeanor assault and battery must be charged within one year.
criminal_felony_assault.citation: W. Va. Code § 61-11-9; W. Va. Code § 61-2-9
criminal_felony_assault.quote: A prosecution for a misdemeanor shall be commenced within one year after the offense was committed
criminal_felony_assault.note: Malicious or unlawful wounding under 61-2-9(a) is a felony. Assault (61-2-9(b)) and battery (61-2-9(c)) are misdemeanors (https://code.wvlegislature.gov/61-2-9/).

channels.name: West Virginia Board of Examiners in Counseling
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses professional counselors and marriage and family therapists in West Virginia and enforces the licensure rules and ethical standards. On a finding of probable cause it can reprimand, suspend or revoke a licence.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It cannot seek or recover any money for the person who complained. Its meetings discussing complaints and investigations are confidential and closed to the public.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed professional counselor or marriage and family therapist in West Virginia.
channels.how: Contact the Board to request a complaint form.
channels.mail: West Virginia Board of Examiners in Counseling, 815 Quarrier Street, Suite 212, Charleston, WV 25301

channels.name: West Virginia Board of Examiners of Psychologists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists in West Virginia.

channels.name: West Virginia Centralized Intake for Abuse and Neglect
channels.what_it_can_do: The single point of entry for every report of suspected abuse and neglect in West Virginia, covering both children and vulnerable adults. Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
channels.who_to_report: A child under 18 at a West Virginia program who is being abused or neglected, or is at risk of it. Anyone concerned for a child can report.
channels.how: Call Centralized Intake, and report to local law enforcement as well. Mandated reporters may also send a non-emergency report by email.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year.

channels.name: West Virginia Department of Human Services, facility complaints
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and regulates West Virginia's residential and behavioral health facilities and takes complaints about them. The state also maintains an abuse registry covering people barred from working in these settings.
channels.how: Contact the Department's complaint line, and report any abuse to Centralized Intake as well.

channels.name: Disability Rights of West Virginia
channels.what_it_can_do: West Virginia's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A West Virginia program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
